llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed local UI patch for OpenClaw's model picker, with limited same-origin browser polling and reversible file changes.

dimensions.detail: The browser script runs in the OpenClaw Control UI page, uses DOM/CSS mutation, localStorage/sessionStorage, a 1-second in-page heartbeat, and same-origin fetch('./') polling every 5 minutes; these are disclosed and aligned with keeping the injected UI enhancement working.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation runs a PowerShell script with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, auto-detects the OpenClaw Control UI directory, backs up index.html, injects one script tag, copies one versioned JS asset, and can remove the patch.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to install, repair, verify, or uninstall the patch; the scope is described clearly, though users should treat installation as an explicit action because it modifies OpenClaw UI files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No OS-level persistence or scheduled task is included in this ClawHub artifact; persistence is limited to the injected local UI asset, index.html tag, localStorage size preference, and timers while the page is open.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The shipped script and documentation match the stated purpose: add a two-column model picker, hide the per-chat account row in that menu, remember picker size, and provide diagnostics.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local patch to OpenClaw's Control UI: it edits index.html, adds a browser script under assets, hides the account row inside the model picker, stores the picker size locally, and may reload an open Control UI tab after detecting a newer same-origin injected build. Use the documented -Remove command to uninstall.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The flagged self-update/self-repair references are disclosed update-detection and reload behavior, plus a GitHub-only scheduled watchdog that is explicitly not part of this artifact; no artifact-backed hidden self-modification was found.
[LP1] expected: The network use is a same-origin browser fetch of './' for update detection, documented in SKILL.md and README; no external network or telemetry path was found.
[P2] unexpected: The hidden-instruction indicators resolved to a UTF-8 BOM and the literal HTML marker used to find the injected script tag, not prompt-injection instructions.
[AE4] expected: The mixed-script content is multilingual documentation and sponsor text; no credential, exfiltration, or hidden command content was found.
[SDI-1] expected: The same-origin polling and automatic reload behavior is real and disclosed; it can interrupt the page, but the code uses version/fingerprint checks and a sessionStorage guard and does not fetch remote payloads.
[SDI-2] expected: The self-update mechanism changes page lifecycle by reloading after a newer injected build is detected; this is purpose-aligned with avoiding stale injected UI code and is documented.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic location.reload() is present after update detection; the skill discloses this behavior and defers while text input is active, so it is a usability risk rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad natural-language install example appears in Chinese documentation, but the install action itself is explicit and the skill documentation describes the file changes before giving the command.
[SQP-3] expected: Fixed Chinese UI strings and multilingual license wording are localization quality issues, not security-relevant unsafe behavior in this artifact.
